tip.title: Because... so...
tip.text: A CAUSE is why something happens. An EFFECT is what happens because of it. Signal words: because, since, so, as a result, that is why, led to. To find a cause, ask "Why did this happen?" To find an effect, ask "What happened because of this?" The cause does not always come first in the sentence, so read the whole thing.

passage.title: Benched
passage.text:
The jeepney drivers went on strike on Monday. Because no jeepneys were running, Paolo had to walk to school. The walk took fifty minutes. He arrived at basketball practice twenty minutes late, sweating and out of breath.

Coach Dizon had one rule: late means you sit. So Paolo sat on the bench for the whole practice. He watched his teammates run the new play without him.

On Tuesday the strike was still on. Paolo did not want to sit again, so he left home at five-thirty in the morning. He got to school early. But he was so tired that in Math he fell asleep and missed the quiz. The teacher gave him a zero.

On Wednesday the strike ended. Paolo rode the jeepney, got to practice on time, and ran the new play with the team. His legs still hurt from two days of walking. But at least his seat on the bench was empty, and he knew the play by heart because he had watched it so many times.

words.meaning: when workers stop working to protest something
words.example: The drivers' strike stopped all the buses.

words.meaning: made to sit out of a game or practice
words.example: The coach benched him for being late.
She knows the song by heart.

items.prompt: Why did Paolo have to walk to school on Monday?
choices: The jeepney drivers were on strike.
items.why: "Because no jeepneys were running, Paolo had to walk to school."

items.prompt: What happened BECAUSE Paolo was late to practice?
choices: He sat on the bench for the whole practice.
items.why: "Late means you sit. So Paolo sat on the bench for the whole practice."

items.prompt: What caused Paolo to get a zero on the Math quiz?
choices: He fell asleep because he had left home so early and was tired.
The teacher did not like him.
items.why: He left at five-thirty to avoid being late, "was so tired that in Math he fell asleep and missed the quiz."

items.prompt: "The jeepney drivers went on strike." What is a strike?
items.why: The result was that no jeepneys were running, so the drivers had stopped working on purpose.

choices: The strike ended and Paolo got to practice on time.
items.why: "On Wednesday the strike ended. Paolo rode the jeepney, got to practice on time..."

items.prompt: How did sitting on the bench end up helping Paolo?
choices: He got to rest his legs.
He watched the new play so many times that he learned it by heart.
items.why: The last sentence says he knew the play "because he had watched it so many times."
